quizzes.stem: A support bot must find the passage that contains the error code E-4012. Which approach is the reliable one?

options.a: A keyword index, because it matches the exact term
options.b: An embedding of every passage, because a code has a meaning like other codes
options.c: Neither, because a code is too short to be indexed at all
options.d: Only a reranker, since the earlier stages cannot see digits

explanation.a: The page says "BM25 is exact. It finds `E-4012` when the query holds it."
explanation.b: Ruled out because an embedding "is weaker with exact strings".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A rare word such as an error code outweighs common words".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the reranker is the optional fifth stage, and the page says the keyword index "finds `E-4012` when the query holds it".

quizzes.stem: A team asks where to get embeddings for Claude-based retrieval. What does the documentation say?

options.a: Use the embedding endpoint of the Messages API, which every model has
options.b: Anthropic offers no model of its own, and names Voyage AI as one provider
options.c: Ask Claude to write the vectors, since it understands the text
options.d: Train a model on the Claude API's logs, which are provided for this

explanation.b: The page quotes "Anthropic does not offer its own embedding model." and names Voyage AI.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Anthropic does not offer its own embedding model", so no endpoint exists.
explanation.c: Ruled out because an embedding model is a trained model that "turns text into a vector of numbers", not a text generator.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the documentation tells you to "assess a variety of embeddings vendors", and says nothing about logs.

quizzes.stem: A cut falls in the middle of a key sentence. What does overlap do about it?

options.a: At least one window holds it whole
options.b: The sentence is dropped from every chunk so that no half survives
options.c: The sentence is stored twice, as a single longer chunk of its own
options.d: The cut moves to the next paragraph without being asked

explanation.a: The page says "with overlap, at least one chunk holds it whole".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "a sentence cut at a boundary loses its meaning on both sides", and overlap keeps it.
explanation.c: Ruled out because each window "repeats the last `overlap` words of the one before it", and does not build a separate chunk.
explanation.d: Ruled out because windows are cut by words: "the last window ends at the last word".

quizzes.stem: Two result lists come from indexes whose scores sit on different scales. How does the fusion method of the practice combine them?

options.a: It adds the raw scores of both indexes and sorts the totals that result
options.b: It sums `1 / (k + rank)` wherever an id appears
options.c: It keeps the longer list and ignores the shorter one completely
options.d: It multiplies each chunk's two scores together before sorting them

explanation.b: The page says "an id's score is the sum, over the lists that hold it, of `1 / (k + rank)`".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "the scores cannot be added" when they are on different scales.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "an id at the top of one list and absent from the other still scores".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Fusion uses only the ranks", with no multiplication of scores.

quizzes.stem: A reranker is given a pool of 10 chunks, and the passage with the answer is ranked 14th by the merged list. What happens?

options.a: The reranker finds it and moves it to the front of the final list
options.b: It is never considered, since the scorer sees only the first ten
options.c: It is added to the candidates when its score is high enough to qualify
options.d: The candidate count is raised for that question by the scorer itself

explanation.b: The page says "Only the pool takes part: a chunk outside it is never considered".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "reranking cannot fix a retrieval that missed".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the pool is "the first `pool` ids of the merged ranking" and nothing is added to it afterwards.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the pool must be large enough to contain the answer", and a scorer has no control over it.

quizzes.stem: A company's reference material has 80,000 tokens and changes once a month. What does the write-up's rule of thumb suggest?

options.a: Skip retrieval, and place everything in a cached prompt
options.b: Build the full pipeline, since every base needs one of its own to work well
options.c: Split it into 20 chunks and index only the first ones that are written
options.d: Train an embedding model of its own on the text of the material

explanation.a: The page says "under about 200,000 tokens, put the whole knowledge base in the prompt and cache it, and skip retrieval".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A pipeline adds stages that can each fail".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the guide for retrieval is to "retrieve 20 chunks rather than fewer", which is a count to retrieve and not a way to index.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "The rule is about size, not quality", and it says nothing about training a model.

quizzes.stem: A question returns a fluent answer from the wrong passage, and the team wants to find which stage failed. What should they do first?

options.a: Measure recall at k on a set with known source documents
options.b: Switch to a larger model and read a few more answers
options.c: Lengthen the prompt with more rules about citing sources
options.d: Raise the temperature to see whether another passage appears

explanation.a: The page says "The way to see it is to measure retrieval on its own", with questions "whose source documents are known".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Fluent output hides that", and a larger model reads the same retrieved passages.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the failure sits in what was retrieved: "the passage with the answer never reached the prompt".
explanation.d: Ruled out because temperature changes the wording of the answer, and "A fluent answer can come from the wrong passage".

quizzes.stem: A passage reads "The company's revenue grew by 3% over the previous quarter" and matches many unrelated questions. Which fix does the write-up describe?

options.a: Prepend a sentence of explanatory context before indexing it
options.b: Shorten it to a single sentence of three or four words
options.c: Delete it and rely on the model's own knowledge of the firm
options.d: Embed it twice and average the two vectors that result

explanation.a: The page says to prepend "chunk-specific explanatory context to each chunk before embedding" and before building the keyword index.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the problem is lost surroundings: "A chunk lifted out of its document can lose its meaning."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the fix keeps the chunk: the model is asked "to write that sentence for each chunk".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the fix is that "the chunk is indexed as a short sentence of context followed by the text", and a doubled vector adds no information.

quizzes.stem: A keyword index and an embedding index disagree on the best chunk for a query. Why is a hybrid usually better than either alone?

options.a: They miss different questions, so a merge keeps what each finds
options.b: Their scores share one scale, which makes adding them a sound choice
options.c: The embedding side handles exact strings well, and the keyword side adds speed
options.d: The merge makes chunking of the documents unnecessary for later stages

explanation.a: The page says "The two indexes fail on different questions, which is why most systems use both."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "the scores cannot be added" when they sit on different scales.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "BM25 is exact", and the embedding "is weaker with exact strings".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A chunk is a window of words", and the merge works on chunks that already exist.

quizzes.stem: A team reads a published failure-rate drop of 67% and promises the same drop to a customer. What is wrong with the promise?

options.a: The figure comes from the source's datasets, and yours needs measuring
options.b: The figure is too small to be useful for any real system that is deployed
options.c: The figure applies only to embeddings, which the customer does not use
options.d: The figure was measured with a retired model that no longer exists

explanation.a: The page says "These are the write-up's figures, measured on its datasets" and "Measure your own."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the figures "show an order of magnitude and a ranking of the techniques".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the 67% row is "Those two, with reranking added", so it is not embeddings alone.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "The percentages for contextual retrieval below are Anthropic's measurements on its own datasets", and the page names no model.
